cards.title: Only one copy of the app runs; launching it again brings the open window forward
cards.user_does: Starts the app (shortcut, Start menu, CLI) while it is already running.
cards.user_sees: No second app appears; the existing window is restored if minimised and brought to the front.
rules: A duplicate launch hands its request to the running copy and exits with a distinct non-zero code.
A minimised window is restored before it is focused; focusing retries briefly when the OS refuses foreground activation.
On Windows the app asks for foreground rights so the window really comes to the front instead of only flashing in the taskbar.
A launch that arrives while no window exists (all closed, still running) opens one window.
acceptance: With the app open and minimised, launch it again → the same window restores and is focused; process count is unchanged.
The duplicate process exits within a few seconds with the duplicate-instance exit code.

cards.title: The main window appears quickly even when the terminal service is slow to start
cards.user_does: Launches the app, including right after a reboot or update.
cards.user_sees: The window shows promptly with the saved layout; terminals reconnect as soon as the background terminal service is ready.
rules: The terminal service and the agent-hook service start in parallel with window creation.
If the terminal service is still not ready after a fixed wait, the first window opens anyway and terminals attach later.
The gate that holds terminal spawning fails open at a hard cap instead of blocking forever.
If the window-ready signal never arrives, the window is revealed on a fallback timer so the user never stares at nothing (Windows and Linux).
Saved UI state loads before projects and worktrees; background polling waits until the workspace session is ready; optional overlays are not loaded at startup.
Terminal reconnect waits for first-window startup services.
Applying the network proxy never delays the first window; it is parked and applied once the window exists.
acceptance: Delay the terminal service start by 30 s → the window still appears within the startup timeout and shows the saved layout; panes fill in once the service is up.
Suppress the window-ready signal → the window becomes visible after the fallback delay.

cards.title: Startup failures and stray background errors do not silently kill the app
cards.user_does: Nothing; a fault happens during launch or while running.
cards.user_sees: A fatal startup failure exits cleanly with a reason in the log instead of leaving a hung process; non-fatal background errors are recorded and the app keeps running.
rules: Unhandled promise rejections and uncaught errors in the main process are logged and swallowed when they are not fatal.
A failure before the first window exists exits the process rather than leaving an invisible app holding the single-instance lock.
acceptance: Inject an unhandled rejection in a background task → the app stays open and the error appears in the local log.
Inject a failure before the window opens → the process exits within seconds and a new launch succeeds.

cards.title: Settings and data from the app's former name are carried over on first launch
cards.user_does: Installs this version over an install that still used the old product name.
cards.user_sees: Projects, settings and history are all there; nothing has to be set up again.
rules: The old profile folder is copied into the new one once; running it again changes nothing.
A file that already exists in the new profile is never overwritten.
Files locked by another process are skipped, not fatal.
The packaged release smoke test checks this migration on every release.
Development and test profiles never receive the migration.
Small UI preferences stored under the former name's prefix are carried over once to the new prefix.
Saved settings stored under the former product's names are renamed to the current names once; a value already saved under the current name is kept, and running the rename again changes nothing.
acceptance: Seed an old-name profile with a project and a setting, launch → both appear; launch again → no duplicate entries.
Pre-create one target file with different content → it is unchanged after migration.
cards.compat: Legacy app-data profile folder Nightshift (any case) is migrated into the Kolux app-data profile folder; data category: full user-data profile.
evidence: src/main/startup/pre-kolux-userdata-migration.test.ts (never migrates into a dev or E2E root)

cards.title: A terminal session can open in its own OS window that remembers where it was (dormant)
cards.user_does: Pops a session out into its own window, moves and resizes it, closes and reopens it later.
cards.user_sees: A separate rounded window showing that one live session; reopening puts it back at the same size and place.
rules: Each session gets at most one window; asking again focuses the existing one (restoring it if minimised).
A different session opens a different window.
Window size and position are saved per session.
Closing one session window leaves every other window and the session itself running.
A window only ever attaches to the terminal it was opened for.
If no terminal id is given, the window attaches to the tab's saved terminal.
Dormant at 0.15.0: nothing in the main UI or the CLI opens a session window; the rounded look of the 10-05 redesign is the in-grid pane card (area 03), not this OS window.
acceptance: Pop out session A, move it, close it, pop it out again → same position and size.
Pop out A and B, close A's window → B's window and both sessions keep running.
evidence: src/main/ipc/terminal-windows.ts:47 (open handler; no renderer caller, only close from inside the window)
cards-raw/21-retired-hidden.json D-21-001 (one OS window per terminal reverted 2026-09-15)

cards.title: Closing the window asks first when work could be lost, and quitting always finishes
cards.user_does: Clicks the window close button or quits from the menu while sessions are running.
cards.user_sees: A confirmation when something would be interrupted; after confirming, the app saves and exits within a bounded time.
rules: The window's own UI decides whether to confirm; the confirmation is skipped only when the UI is gone or crashed.
A quit has a deadline: if teardown hangs, the app exits anyway after saving what it can.
On Windows and Linux closing the last window quits; on macOS the app stays running unless a quit is already committed.
Closing a pop-out session window never triggers the main window's quit flow.
A UI that is hung but still alive is still asked to confirm; only a UI whose process is gone lets the window close without asking.
acceptance: With a running agent, click close → confirmation appears; cancel → window stays; confirm → app exits.
Make the UI unresponsive and quit → app still exits within the quit deadline.

cards.title: Optional: closing the window hides the app to the tray instead of quitting (Windows)
cards.user_does: Turns on the minimise-to-tray option, then clicks the window close button.
cards.user_sees: The window disappears but the app keeps running in the tray; the first time, a notification explains where it went.
rules: Off by default.
The explanatory notification is shown once only.
A real quit (menu, tray Quit, OS shutdown) is never intercepted.
Windows session end (logoff, shutdown) is recorded so the next launch knows it was not a crash.
acceptance: Option on, click close → window hidden, process alive, tray icon present; first time only, a notification appears.
Option on, choose Quit from the tray → app exits.

cards.title: Tray icon with a small menu and an attention dot
cards.user_does: Looks at or clicks the tray icon.
cards.user_sees: A tray icon; its menu offers Open Kolux and Quit. A dot appears on the icon when a bell or an agent finishing happened while the window was hidden.
rules: Windows and macOS only; Linux has no tray icon.
Left-click on Windows opens the app.
Development copies show a DEV label and which branch they run from.
The attention dot clears when the window is shown.
acceptance: Hide the window, let an agent finish → the tray icon shows the dot; open the window → dot clears.
Left-click the tray icon on Windows → main window shows.

cards.title: Standard application menu bar: File, View, Window, Help
cards.user_does: Opens the menu bar menus.
cards.user_sees: File (Settings, Exit), View (reload, force reload, developer tools, reset size, zoom in and out, full screen), Window (minimise, zoom), Help (report a crash, explore the app, getting started, and on Windows/Linux About and Check for Updates).
rules: On macOS the app menu holds About, Check for Updates, Settings, Services, hide and quit items instead of File.
Help → Report Crash reopens the latest crash report even if it was dismissed.
Menu accelerators match the in-app shortcuts.
Edit menu on every platform: Undo, Redo, Cut, Copy, Paste and Select All; copy, paste and select-all act on whichever surface has focus (terminal, editor or text field).

The View menu also carries the workspace-view switch (Agents, Board, Terminals) and an Appearance submenu of sidebar and button toggles; those belong to area 05, except Show Titlebar App Name (see the window look card).

On macOS the hiding group in the app menu runs, in order, Hide (Kolux itself), Hide Others (every other app's windows go while Kolux stays on screen) and Show All (every hidden app comes back); each is the operating system's stock action and the app adds no logic of its own.
acceptance: On Windows open Help → Check for Updates is present and starts a check showing the update card.
View → zoom in increases the UI zoom; reset size restores it.
evidence: registry:menu-items:darwin only|macOS app menu (label=app.name or appMenuLabel)|Hide Others
registry:menu-items:darwin only|macOS app menu (label=app.name or appMenuLabel)|Show All (unhide)

cards.title: Settings and Help menu in the sidebar footer
cards.user_does: Opens the settings/help menu at the bottom of the sidebar.
cards.user_sees: Settings, plus Help with Docs, Changelog, GitHub, Milestones, Keyboard Shortcuts, Onboarding, Send Feedback, Copy terminal diagnostics, Check for Updates and Restart Kolux.
rules: Restart Kolux shows a restarting state and relaunches the app after saving.
Copy terminal diagnostics puts a redacted diagnostic summary on the clipboard.
Docs, Changelog and GitHub open in the system browser.
acceptance: Choose Restart Kolux → app relaunches with the same layout and sessions.
Choose Copy terminal diagnostics → clipboard holds text without secrets or home paths.

cards.title: Restart, reload and update never run before the current state is safely saved
cards.user_does: Clicks Restart Kolux, Restart to update, or a reload.
cards.user_sees: The app saves, then restarts; if saving fails, the restart is refused and the app stays as it was.
rules: Every destructive app action (relaunch, quit-and-install, reload) waits for a durable save checkpoint first.
A failed checkpoint cancels the action rather than risking lost layout or sessions.
Recovery reloads after a failed lazy-loaded screen reuse the same checkpoint.

If the full snapshot of the current state fails, the last durable save is used and the action continues when nothing unsaved would be lost; with unsaved editor drafts the action is refused and the drafts stay.
acceptance: Make the save fail, click Restart Kolux → app does not restart and reports the failure.
Normal restart → the restored layout matches the pre-restart layout exactly.

cards.title: App icon choice and window look options
cards.user_does: Picks an app icon variant, turns window background blur on, or hides the app name in the title bar.
cards.user_sees: The taskbar/dock icon changes to the chosen variant (classic, watercolor or blue); the window background blurs; the title bar shows or hides the app name.
rules: An unknown icon choice falls back to the default icon.
Background blur is off by default; the app name in the title bar is on by default.
acceptance: Choose the blue icon → taskbar icon switches without restart (or on next launch where the OS requires it).
Toggle the title bar name off → the name disappears from the title bar.

cards.title: Zoom and tab-switch shortcuts work wherever focus is
cards.user_does: Presses zoom in/out/reset, Ctrl+Tab or a tab-number shortcut while typing in a terminal or the editor.
cards.user_sees: The app zooms or switches tabs instead of the keystroke being swallowed by the focused terminal or editor.
rules: Window-level shortcuts are intercepted before the page sees them.
Terminal-focus shortcuts and markdown-editor focus are routed to the right surface.
acceptance: Focus a terminal, press Ctrl+Tab → next tab activates; the terminal receives no characters.
Press zoom in twice then reset → UI zoom returns to 100 %.

cards.title: Right-click menu in text fields with spelling suggestions and edit actions
cards.user_does: Right-clicks inside a text box or the rich-text editor.
cards.user_sees: Spelling suggestions when available, cut/copy/paste, and table actions when the cursor is inside a table.
rules: No menu outside editable text.
Plain inputs get spelling and native edit actions only; table actions only appear inside a table.
Suggestions appear even if spellcheck is reported off when the engine still offers them.
acceptance: Right-click a misspelled word in a text field → suggestions listed; choose one → word replaced.
Right-click plain text outside an input → no app context menu.

cards.title: Web links open in the system browser; the app window can never be navigated away
cards.user_does: Clicks a link in a terminal, a note or a dialog.
cards.user_sees: The link opens in the default browser (or in the in-app browser where that is the chosen route); the app stays on its own screen.
rules: Any attempt to navigate the main window to an outside web address is blocked and handed to the browser.
Foreign file hosts and data addresses that imitate the app's own pages are blocked.
Embedded preview pages only load addresses the app has granted; grants are cleared when the window is recreated.
Links from floating workspaces open in the app without switching the active worktree.
A modifier-click inverts the chosen link route, and the system browser stays reachable when links normally open inside the app.
acceptance: Click an https link in a terminal → default browser opens it; app window unchanged.
Script a navigation of the main window to an outside address → blocked.

cards.title: Clipboard works for files, images and verified text
cards.user_does: Copies a file from the app to paste into another program, pastes an image into a terminal, or copies text.
cards.user_sees: The file pastes elsewhere as a real file; a pasted image arrives as a file the agent can read (with a thumbnail); copied text is exactly what was selected.
rules: Only absolute paths inside allowed local roots can be put on the clipboard as files.
Each platform uses its own file-clipboard method; on Linux several tools are tried and unsupported is reported if none works.
Text writes are read back and must match exactly (line endings included) or the copy is reported as failed.
Pasted images are saved to a temporary file that is cleaned up later.
acceptance: Copy a file from the explorer, paste into the OS file manager → the file is copied.
Copy multi-line text with CRLF → pasted text is byte-identical.

cards.title: After sleep the window repaints, and hidden windows stop doing UI work
cards.user_does: Wakes the computer from sleep, or leaves the window minimised for a long time.
cards.user_sees: The window is drawn correctly right after wake; a minimised app uses little CPU and catches up instantly when shown.
rules: System resume triggers a repaint of every window.
Live updates to hidden windows are parked and replayed when the window becomes visible.
Updates to the UI are throttled so bursts do not freeze it.
Hidden windows are exempt from the browser engine's aggressive background-timer throttling, so status updates keep arriving while minimised.
acceptance: Sleep and wake the machine → no blank or stale regions in the window.
Minimise for 10 minutes with agents running → on restore, status reflects the current state within one second.
evidence: src/main/startup/configure-process.test.ts (opts hidden pages out of intensive wake-up throttling)

cards.title: Optional: keep the computer awake while agents are running
cards.user_does: Turns on the keep-awake option and leaves agents working.
cards.user_sees: The computer does not go to sleep while any agent is running; normal sleep resumes when they stop.
rules: Off by default.
macOS and Linux hold an OS sleep inhibitor (Linux also blocks lid-close sleep); only one inhibitor at a time.
If the inhibitor tool is missing it degrades to doing nothing and logs once.
Windows behaviour not confirmed from tests.
acceptance: Option on, agent running → OS reports a sleep inhibitor held by the app; agent stops → inhibitor released.

cards.title: Markdown files opened from the OS open inside the app
cards.user_does: Double-clicks or uses Open with on a markdown file outside the app.
cards.user_sees: The app comes forward and shows the file in its editor, even if it was not running yet.
rules: Files requested before the window is ready are queued and delivered once it is.
Non-markdown files are ignored.
A file handed over as an encoded file address (for example with spaces in the path) is decoded so it still opens.
acceptance: With the app closed, open a .md file with it → app starts and the file is open in the editor.

cards.title: Terminals see the same tools as the user's shell, including newly installed ones
cards.user_does: Installs a CLI (for example an agent) and opens a new terminal or session.
cards.user_sees: The new tool is found without restarting the computer.
rules: At startup the app reads the user's login shell environment and search path.
On Windows the persisted user and system path are re-read; entries installed after the app started are kept.
A change of configured shell re-reads the path for that shell; queued changes collapse to the latest.
Agent detection refresh re-reads the path before checking again; if the shell cannot start it falls back to the current path.
In installed copies, Node version-manager folders are placed ahead of the system folders on the search path, so the runtime the user chose wins over a system install.
acceptance: Install a CLI while the app runs, open a new terminal → the CLI runs by name.
Refresh agent detection after installing an agent → it is detected.

cards.title: Broken install-folder permissions are detected and repaired on Windows
cards.user_does: Launches after an install or update left the install or profile folder with wrong permissions.
cards.user_sees: The app starts normally; when it cannot repair, the recovery prompt names a permissions problem instead of crashing repeatedly.
rules: A quick probe at startup checks that the install folder and profile folder are writable by the user.
Repairs are applied to the user's own install only.
Graphics-process failures caused by unreadable install files are treated as a permission problem, not a GPU crash.
acceptance: Remove the user's access to a file in the install folder, launch → access restored and app starts.

cards.title: More memory headroom for the UI on larger machines
cards.user_does: Runs many sessions on a machine with 8 GB of RAM or more.
cards.user_sees: The UI does not run out of memory as early; an environment variable can set the limit explicitly.
rules: Below 8 GB of RAM the default limit is kept.
An explicit value from the environment wins over the automatic choice.
acceptance: Launch with the override set to a value → the UI process uses that heap limit.

cards.title: Landing screen flags missing or signed-out tools before the user starts
cards.user_does: Opens the app on the landing screen.
cards.user_sees: Notices when Git is missing, when the GitHub CLI is missing or not signed in, or when agent CLIs are missing; each notice can be dismissed.
rules: Git problems are always shown; GitHub CLI problems only when a GitHub-backed project exists.
GitLab CLI is reported as not installed when its version check fails.
A dismissed notice stays dismissed until the set of GitHub projects changes.
Probes that hang are timed out; results are cached and a manual refresh re-probes.
acceptance: Remove git from the path, open the landing screen → a Git notice appears.
Dismiss the GitHub CLI notice, restart → it stays dismissed; add a new GitHub project → it returns.

cards.title: The app checks for updates at launch and every 30 minutes, quietly
cards.user_does: Leaves the app running.
cards.user_sees: Nothing while checking; a new version is found within about half an hour of being published.
rules: Checks at launch if the last check is older than the interval, otherwise waits for the rest of the interval; then every 30 minutes.
Updates come from the public releases repository on GitHub, which holds installers only.
Checks triggered by window focus are de-duplicated.
After a failed check it retries after about an hour, doubling up to six hours.
While offline it stays quiet and checks within about a minute of the connection returning.
After waking from sleep it checks if the last check is stale.
A stalled check is abandoned after a timeout.
Background checks never show errors; Windows signature verification is never turned off.
Updates do not run in development or unpackaged copies.
acceptance: Publish a new release, leave the app open → within 30 minutes the update downloads without any click.
Disconnect the network for an hour → no error shown; reconnect → a check runs within about a minute.
cards.compat: Update feed: GitHub releases of TxaisX/kolux-releases with latest.yml.

cards.title: A downloaded update shows a small ready pop-up and installs on restart or next quit
cards.user_does: Keeps working after an update has downloaded in the background.
cards.user_sees: A small pop-up in the bottom-left says the new version is ready, with Restart to update and a close button. Ignoring it is fine: the update installs next time the app quits.
rules: The download starts on its own, without a click.
The pop-up shows once per version per launch and stays until acted on or closed.
If the update card is already showing the update, the pop-up stays silent.
The pop-up disappears when the update is no longer ready.
The app never restarts itself for an update; the user must click or quit.
acceptance: After a background download → pop-up appears once; close it → it does not return this launch.
Quit the app without clicking → next launch runs the new version.

cards.title: Update card shows the progress of a check the user asked for
cards.user_does: Clicks Check for Updates.
cards.user_sees: A card showing checking, up to date (then fades away), update available, downloading with progress, ready with Restart to update, or an error with a way forward.
rules: Background checks never show the card; only user-initiated checks and download errors do.
A version the user dismissed stays hidden until a newer one appears.
The card can be collapsed; every phase change brings it back.
After download the card waits for the user to click Restart; it never installs without consent.
Escape minimises the card; Enter runs its main action; reduced-motion turns off its animations.
Repeated clicks while a check is running do not start a second check.
A check that never reaches the update engine times out and says so.

The first time an update is offered or downloading, a small dismissible tip above the card says running terminal sessions won't be interrupted; it disappears for good once dismissed or once the user starts a download.
If the user asks for a check while a quiet background check is already running, that check is promoted so the user sees its result in the card.
acceptance: Click Check for Updates on the latest version → card says up to date and dismisses itself.
With an update available, dismiss the card → it does not return for that version; publish a newer one → it returns.
evidence: src/main/updater.check-settlement.test.ts (keeps a silent background settle user-initiated after menu promotion)

cards.title: Release notes appear in the update card
cards.user_does: Sees an available or downloaded update in the card.
cards.user_sees: A short list of what changed in that version, taken from the release's notes.
rules: Notes are read from the public release page without signing in.
Headings and blank lines are dropped and the list is capped to a few lines.
Any failure (offline, missing release) simply shows no notes; it never blocks the update.
Notes are kept through available, downloading, ready and error, and cleared when a new check cycle starts.
acceptance: Publish a release with five bullet notes → card lists them; disconnect before the notes load → card shows without notes and the update still works.

cards.title: If an update failed to install, the next launch says so and offers a retry
cards.user_does: Restarts to update, but the install does not take (for example a file was locked).
cards.user_sees: On the next launch a notice explains the update did not install, names the program holding files when known, and offers Try again or Download installer. When it worked, a one-time note says the app was updated, with the notes.
rules: The app records each install attempt and compares it with the running version on the next launch.
Records older than seven days are ignored.
Deliberate jumps to a pinned or locally built version are never reported as failures.
When no locking program can be identified, generic wording is used.
acceptance: Lock an install file, restart to update → next launch shows the failure notice with Try again.
Successful update → one-time updated note with notes; it does not reappear on the following launch.

cards.title: Restart to update always either installs or tells the user why it could not
cards.user_does: Clicks Restart to update.
cards.user_sees: The app saves, closes and the new version starts; if the installer cannot run, the app stays open with the real reason (for example missing permission).
rules: Cleanup before quitting has a short time limit so the restart is not delayed.
A watchdog forces the old process to exit at its deadline so the installer is not blocked; re-arming never extends the deadline.
If the install fails immediately, the watchdog is disarmed and the app stays usable.
The reported cause is the underlying one, with paths and secrets removed.
Clicking Restart to update again while the app is already preparing to quit is ignored; only one install runs.
acceptance: Normal update → old process gone within the deadline and new version running.
Deny elevation → app stays open and the error names a permission problem.

cards.title: An update whose Windows signature does not match is stopped, never offered for bypass
cards.user_does: Receives an update whose installer signature does not match the installed app.
cards.user_sees: A security stop card explaining the update was refused; there is no button to install it anyway.
rules: The rejected version is never offered again for install.
Applies only to signed builds; current releases are unsigned, so this path is not normally reached.
acceptance: Serve an update signed by a different publisher to a signed build → security stop card, no install option.

cards.title: Update download problems recover on their own or offer a fix
cards.user_does: Checks for updates on a network that breaks downloads, or while a release is still being published.
cards.user_sees: For network-protocol errors the card offers to switch to a compatibility mode and retry; during publishing the app keeps the last good release and checks again shortly.
rules: A release whose files are not all uploaded yet is skipped in favour of the last complete one, retried on a short cadence.
A missing update manifest is treated as a quiet no-update, not an error.
Stale events from an earlier check never overwrite the current check's result.
Local-build errors never send the user to a platform download page.

Background checks stay quiet about a mid-publish feed or a missing platform manifest; a check the user asked for shows a calm plain-language explanation instead of the raw error, and no rapid retry is scheduled.
An environment variable can force the network compatibility mode on or off, overriding the saved setting.
If the newest complete release cannot be worked out, the check falls back to the repository's latest release.
acceptance: Publish a release with the manifest but no installer yet → app does not error and picks it up once the installer is uploaded.
Force an HTTP/2 protocol error during a manual check → card offers compatibility mode; accept → next check succeeds.

cards.title: Network proxy can be set for the app's own traffic
cards.user_does: Enters a proxy address and bypass list, optionally with a username and password.
cards.user_sees: Update checks and other app traffic go through the proxy; clearing it returns to the system proxy.
rules: Explicit settings win, then the system proxy, then proxy environment variables.
Proxy credentials are stored as a secret, survive restart, are never shown in metadata and are only sent to the matching proxy.
Changes apply in order; a failed application keeps requests blocked rather than leaking around the proxy.
Its settings section is folded: the knob moves to General.
A bypass list names hosts that skip the proxy.
If the saved proxy address cannot be decrypted (for example after an OS key change), it is left sealed and unused rather than erased.
acceptance: Set a proxy with credentials, restart → update check goes through the proxy with the credentials.
Clear the proxy → traffic goes direct or through the system proxy.

cards.title: Alternative update channels and modifier-click prerelease checks
cards.user_does: Shift-clicks or Ctrl-clicks Check for Updates, or switches to an hourly/daily/ad-hoc build channel.
cards.user_sees: A check against release-candidate or performance prerelease feeds, or a list of hourly/daily builds newest first.
rules: Shift = release candidate; Ctrl (Cmd on macOS) = performance prerelease; a tooltip hints this per platform.
A Shift-click during a running stable check starts a fresh prerelease check.
Builds without a file for this platform are hidden; rate limits give an actionable message.
Dev channels exist on Windows and macOS only; leaving a signed build for one needs a manual install.
Kolux publishes a single channel, so these feeds are not populated.
acceptance: n/a — decision item

cards.title: Switching to a locally built version, and updates in unpackaged copies
cards.user_does: A developer points the app at a locally built package, or runs an unpackaged copy and checks for updates.
cards.user_sees: The local build is offered like an update and installed; an unpackaged copy explains it cannot install updates.
rules: The local package must match its hash, contain no links or path escapes, and have exactly one archive for this machine's architecture.
It is served from a private local feed that only answers tokenized requests.
A local build whose saved-state or live-terminal protocol is incompatible is refused.
Local-build selection takes precedence over channel modifiers; local versions never link to GitHub downloads.
acceptance: n/a — decision item

cards.title: Linux-only update and launch paths
cards.user_does: Runs the app from a Linux package or AppImage.
cards.user_sees: Package-managed installs report a new version but do not download it; a recovery card offers a copy-able install command, reveal-file and a link to the release. The AppImage runs CLI commands when given one.
rules: Enable & Restart relaunches only once even if double-clicked.
Package-manager commands are built only for trusted package managers and quoted safely; diagnostics are redacted.
Linux builds are not released, so none of this reaches users today.
A stale command-line registration left by a moved or older AppImage is repaired, and the CLI then reports as installed.
acceptance: n/a — decision item

cards.title: macOS-only startup and window behaviour
cards.user_does: Runs the app on macOS.
cards.user_sees: Key repeat works in terminals (press-and-hold accent popup turned off unless the user set it), a notice explains repeated macOS permission prompts, Full Disk Access is detected, a menu-bar icon follows light/dark appearance, and maximised windows render correctly on newer macOS.
rules: An explicit user choice for press-and-hold is respected; failures leave the decision open.
The menu-bar icon can be turned off.
macOS builds are not released, so none of this reaches users today.

A terminal service left over from a macOS login session that has ended is retired so the next launch starts a fresh one; it is retired only after repeated failed login checks plus a confirmed broken system name resolver, never on an inconclusive check, and the resolver check never stalls live terminals.
acceptance: n/a — decision item

cards.title: Send Feedback opens a pre-filled GitHub issue for the user to review
cards.user_does: Chooses Send Feedback, types a message, optionally ticks Submit anonymously, clicks Open on GitHub.
cards.user_sees: The browser opens a new-issue page on the project's GitHub with title and body filled in; the app itself sends nothing.
rules: The title is prefixed as feedback and uses the first line of the message, capped at 80 characters; empty text is refused with an error.
The body adds app version, platform, OS release and architecture, and the GitHub login unless anonymous is ticked.
Paths and secrets are scrubbed from the text.
Very long reports are cut to fit a browser address, with a note saying so.
No network request is made by the app; the browser does the submission.
acceptance: Send feedback with text → browser opens a new-issue page with a [Feedback] title and the version in the body.
Tick Submit anonymously → the body has no GitHub login.
cards.compat: Issue target: https://github.com/TxaisX/kolux/issues/new with title and body query parameters.

cards.title: Screenshots can be added to feedback and are put on the clipboard for pasting
cards.user_does: Adds screenshots to a feedback report.
cards.user_sees: Up to four images attach; when the issue page opens, the first screenshot is already on the clipboard ready to paste, with a note of how many there are.
rules: PNG, JPEG, WebP or GIF only; at most 4 images, at most 8 MB each.
Crash reports do not take images; they copy the redacted diagnostic bundle instead.
An empty image is rejected as soon as it is added, not at submit time.
A file whose contents are not a valid image is rejected with a message naming it, gets no preview and does not count toward the limit.
Adding images past the limit adds none of the extra ones and tells the user the limit.
acceptance: Attach five images → the fifth is refused.
Attach one PNG and submit → pasting into the issue page inserts that image.

cards.title: After a crash the app offers to report it as a GitHub issue
cards.user_does: Relaunches after a crash, or picks Help → Report Crash.
cards.user_sees: Once, at startup, a crash report dialog with Attach recent diagnostic logs, Copy Details and Open on GitHub; when nothing was captured it says so.
rules: Only the latest pending report prompts, once; it is then marked dismissed.
Help → Report Crash reopens the latest report even if dismissed.
Attaching logs copies a redacted log bundle to the clipboard for pasting into the issue.
Issue titles are prefixed as a crash report.
Clipboard failures show a toast instead of failing silently.
acceptance: Force a renderer crash, relaunch → dialog appears once; relaunch again → no dialog.
Help → Report Crash after dismissing → the same report opens.

cards.title: Only real crashes are recorded, with useful context
cards.user_does: Nothing; processes exit during normal use or shutdown.
cards.user_sees: No false crash prompts after normal quits or deliberate kills; genuine crash reports include memory conditions just before the crash.
rules: Exits during expected teardown, graphics exits at shutdown and kills the app issued itself are not reported as crashes; renderer crashes and unknown child crashes still are.
Only the newest five reports are kept; reports from the same crash are merged and siblings dismissed.
Crash dumps that arrive late are merged into the existing report.
The store survives corrupt files (starts empty) and retries saves on Windows when files are briefly locked.
The last host memory reading before the crash is attached, never claiming free disk as proof swap could grow.
When a crash dump is available, the report names the faulting module.
acceptance: Quit normally 10 times → no crash prompt.
Crash the renderer 7 times → only five reports exist.

cards.title: Diagnostic logs stay local and are scrubbed of secrets before they leave the app
cards.user_does: Copies terminal diagnostics or attaches logs to a crash report.
cards.user_sees: Useful logs on the clipboard with API keys, passwords, tokens, credentials in web addresses and .env values replaced.
rules: Logs are written to rotating local files readable only by the user, with a cap on total size.
The bundle includes the terminal-service lifecycle log.
Redaction covers key-value pairs, command-line secrets, environment-style lines, credentials in URLs and blocklisted keys; redacting twice changes nothing.
A review file can be created, opened and discarded before sharing.
Recording diagnostics can never make the action being recorded fail.
acceptance: Put a fake API key in a terminal command, copy diagnostics → the key is not in the clipboard text.
Generate logs beyond the cap → oldest files are removed and total size stays under the cap.

cards.title: When the UI crashes or a screen fails to load, the app recovers or asks what to do
cards.user_does: Keeps working when the UI process crashes, hangs while reloading, or a screen fails to load after an update.
cards.user_sees: The UI reloads on its own; if that fails, a prompt names the likely cause and offers Reload or Quit, with commands to copy. A screen that failed to load offers a reload instead of a blank area.
rules: One automatic recovery reload; if it never produces a page it retries once, then shows the prompt.
Error pages do not count as a successful reload; a stall budget restarts after the machine wakes.
A recovery prompt is never stacked on another, and is not shown for a window already closing.
Repeated recoveries are counted and a circuit breaker stops reload loops.
Causes named include stalled reloads, install permission problems and graphics driver hints.
Before a recovery reload, unsaved editor buffers are backed up; if they cannot be backed up, the reload is refused.
acceptance: Kill the UI process → it reloads automatically with layout intact.
Make the reload hang twice → the prompt appears with Reload and Quit.

cards.title: Repeated graphics crashes switch the app to safe graphics, with the user's consent
cards.user_does: Hits a burst of graphics-process crashes on Windows.
cards.user_sees: A prompt offering to restart in safe graphics mode, or Keep Running. On the next launch a choice between staying in safe graphics and retrying hardware acceleration.
rules: Triggered by a burst of crashes within a short window, at most once.
The safe-graphics marker is saved before the prompt is answered; Keep Running removes it.
Safe graphics is the default choice on the recovered launch; the choice is remembered.
The marker is cleared when the app version changes and ignored off Windows.
acceptance: Simulate three graphics crashes in a minute → restart prompt; accept → app relaunches in safe graphics.
Update the app → hardware acceleration is tried again.

cards.title: Main-thread hang watchdog
cards.user_does: Nothing; the app's main process freezes for a while.
cards.user_sees: Nothing on Windows. On macOS a background watcher records the stall and whether it cleared, for diagnostics only.
rules: Runs only on macOS; a no-op elsewhere.
A large gap in timing is treated as system sleep, not a hang.
One record per stall; only reported through the disabled telemetry path.
acceptance: n/a — decision item

cards.title: Usage telemetry is compiled off
cards.user_does: Uses the app.
cards.user_sees: No usage data is sent; the privacy statement says this build sends none.
rules: The telemetry client is disabled at build time regardless of settings.
Consent, install id, cohort classification, rate caps and event schema validation exist but never transmit.
The privacy settings section is folded per the owner cut; there is no knob.
acceptance: n/a — decision item

cards.title: Diagnostic upload is unavailable and can be refused by environment
cards.user_does: Looks for a diagnostic upload option, or sets an opt-out variable.
cards.user_sees: Upload reports not available in this build; opt-out variables and CI environments disable it in any case.
rules: Upload addresses are validated before any upload; bundles have submission ids and can be deleted.
Opt-out variables do not change the saved setting.
acceptance: n/a — decision item

cards.title: Typing-latency and main-thread churn probes
cards.user_does: A developer enables performance diagnostics.
cards.user_sees: Summaries of typing latency and of subprocess spawning on the main thread in the logs.
rules: Off for normal users; sample windows and summaries only.
acceptance: n/a — decision item

cards.title: Everything the user set up is saved continuously and survives quits and updates
cards.user_does: Arranges projects, sessions and settings, then quits, updates or restarts.
cards.user_sees: The same projects, layout, sessions and settings on the next launch.
rules: Saves are atomic (write then rename) and run off the UI thread.
Identical state is not rewritten; real changes, including secret changes, always are.
Older saved formats and keys are migrated forward; retired settings are removed.
Brief database contention is retried; read-only opens survive another writer.
A saved session from the previous production version restores after upgrading.
The profile folder and its private files are restricted to the current user, on Windows as well.
Saved settings with some invalid entries keep the valid ones, drop the rest, and the repaired version is written back.

After an upgrade, an install that existed before the new workspace screens and never chose one keeps opening on the terminal grid; a fresh install gets the new default, an explicit choice is never overwritten, and an unreadable saved file counts as an existing install.
acceptance: Change a setting and kill the process two seconds later → setting present on relaunch.
Upgrade from the previous release → layout and sessions identical.
cards.compat: Saved profile state (layout, projects, sessions, settings) must be importable from the 0.15 profile.

cards.title: A corrupt saved-state file never wipes the user's setup
cards.user_does: Launches after the main state file was damaged (crash mid-write, disk issue).
cards.user_sees: The app starts from the last good safety copy; if it cannot protect the damaged file, it stops saving rather than overwrite it.
rules: The damaged file is copied aside before anything is restored.
If it cannot be copied aside and cannot be read, saves are frozen for the session.
An empty (zero-byte) file is treated as missing, not frozen.
acceptance: Corrupt the state file, launch → previous setup restored from the safety copy and the damaged file kept aside.
Make the folder read-only and corrupt the file → app runs without overwriting it.

cards.title: Quitting writes a final save without freezing the app
cards.user_does: Quits the app or restarts to update.
cards.user_sees: The app closes promptly, and everything up to the moment of quitting is there next time.
rules: The final save is one barrier: any pending save is finished first, and nothing schedules another afterwards.
No synchronous disk work on the quit path; a stalled drive cannot hang the app.
The quit deadline bounds a stuck save.
Usage statistics close out live agents before the final write.
Leftover temp files are swept before the final write.
If the profile drive refuses writes, quit continues instead of erroring.
acceptance: Change layout and quit immediately → change restored on relaunch.
Simulate a stalled profile drive → app still exits within the quit deadline.

cards.title: Stale worktree records are cleaned up safely
cards.user_does: Deletes worktrees outside the app, or reopens the app after folders moved.
cards.user_sees: Gone worktrees without sessions disappear from the saved list; worktrees with sessions or on unreachable drives are kept.
rules: Only records with no session and a confirmed-missing folder are pruned.
Unreachable storage is never treated as missing.
Sessions are kept separately per host so one machine's entries never overwrite another's.
acceptance: Delete a worktree folder that has no session, relaunch → it is gone from the list.
Disconnect a drive holding a worktree, relaunch → the worktree is still listed.

cards.title: Terminals survive app restarts and a replaced terminal service
cards.user_does: Quits and relaunches the app, updates it, or the background terminal service is killed or replaced.
cards.user_sees: Running terminals come back with their output; nothing typed goes to the wrong terminal.
rules: Each terminal service instance has a generation; input is always routed to the generation that owns the terminal.
The UI waits for the service to adopt existing terminals before recovering, failing open at a hard cap.
A newer desktop talking to an older service keeps working where changes are additive; incompatible versions are refused.
Events from a replaced service generation are ignored.
Verified across three quit-relaunch cycles and a killed service.
acceptance: Print a marker in a terminal, quit and relaunch three times → marker still visible each time.
Kill the terminal service, relaunch → terminals restored from saved history.

cards.title: Closing a terminal or the app leaves no orphaned processes
cards.user_does: Closes a terminal or kills a session.
cards.user_sees: The shell and every program it started stop; nothing keeps running invisibly.
rules: On Windows each terminal's processes are grouped so the whole group ends together.
If grouping is refused by the OS it degrades gracefully and falls back to killing the process tree.
Kills the app issues itself are logged so they are not mistaken for crashes.
acceptance: Start a long-running child process in a terminal, close the terminal → the child process is gone within seconds.

cards.title: Resource Manager shows memory per session and can kill one
cards.user_does: Opens the Resource Manager from the status bar, looks at usage, kills a session or restarts the terminal service.
cards.user_sees: Memory and CPU for the app, each session grouped by worktree, and terminals not tied to any worktree; a confirmation before a kill; host memory available.
rules: Each terminal's process tree is counted once; a subtree already counted for another terminal is not double-counted.
Terminals with no worktree go into a separate group.
Host available memory uses each OS's own notion (memory pressure on macOS, available memory on Linux).
Killing a session that is not bound to a pane never affects other sessions.
If a process row is missing, the app's own working set is used as a fallback.
CPU figures are capped at the machine's total core capacity, so a sampling glitch never shows an impossible percentage.
acceptance: Open the popover with three sessions → three rows with memory figures.
Kill one after confirming → only that session ends.

cards.title: kolux diagnostics memory prints a memory snapshot
cards.user_does: Runs the memory diagnostics command, optionally with JSON output.
cards.user_sees: Memory for the app and each managed terminal, the same figures as the Resource Manager.
rules: JSON output is machine-readable for scripts and agents.
On Windows the process sweep is sampled efficiently and parsed robustly.
acceptance: Run it with JSON output while two terminals run → valid JSON with two terminal entries.

cards.title: kolux open launches the app and waits until it is ready
cards.user_does: Runs the open command from a terminal or script.
cards.user_sees: The app starts (or comes forward) and the command returns once the app can take further commands.
rules: Works whether or not the app is already running.
JSON output reports readiness for scripts.
acceptance: With the app closed, run it → app opens and the command exits successfully after the runtime is reachable.

cards.title: kolux status reports whether the app and its runtime are ready
cards.user_does: Runs the status command.
cards.user_sees: Whether the app is running, whether its runtime is reachable, and whether its data is loaded.
rules: JSON output is available for scripts and agents.
acceptance: With the app closed → status says not running; open it → status reports ready.

cards.title: One ship command commits, syncs and lands work on main
cards.user_does: Runs the ship command from a worktree, optionally targeting main.
cards.user_sees: Changes committed with an AI-written message, merged with the latest remote, pushed; targeting main also starts a release in the background.
rules: Pulls by merge, never rebase; a conflict aborts with nothing pushed.
A custom message can be given instead of the AI one (used for version-bump commits).
Options: skip the release, merge a named branch, dry run, choose the message model.
acceptance: Ship to main with a change → commit on main, pushed, and a release job log path printed.
Ship with a merge conflict → aborts and the remote is unchanged.

cards.title: Every ship to main publishes a new release automatically
cards.user_does: Ships to main.
cards.user_sees: Minutes later a new numbered release appears in the public releases repository, and installed apps pick it up.
rules: The release builds in its own dedicated checkout; it never touches anyone's working folder and the shipped worktree can be removed straight away.
Only one build at a time; a ship during a build asks for one more build from the newest main. Locks older than three hours or with a dead process are stale.
Version is one patch above the larger of the project version and the latest release; the installed app, the update manifest and the CLI version all agree.

Published: the Windows installer, its block map and the update manifest. Notes are the commit subjects since the last release (at most 30) plus a hidden source marker so an already-released main is skipped.
A failed release is logged and never fails the ship.
Rehearsal modes: print-only, or build and smoke-test without publishing.
Versioning: 0.x.y — x for new capability, y for improvements; never 1.0 without the owner.
No in-app rollback; only Windows is released.
acceptance: Ship to main → a release one patch higher appears with the three files and notes listing the shipped commits.
Ship twice quickly → exactly two builds run in sequence, no parallel builds.
cards.compat: Release assets: kolux-windows-setup.exe, its .blockmap, latest.yml; kolux --version reports the release version; KOLUX_RELEASE_WORKTREE overrides the build checkout; release job flags --dry-run and --no-publish.

cards.title: Continuous integration on main runs in four shards and gates releases
cards.user_does: Pushes to main.
cards.user_sees: The test suite runs split four ways and reports green or red.
rules: A release built through CI refuses to publish unless CI succeeded for that exact commit, waiting up to 30 minutes for a queued run.
The reason for a refusal is written to the job summary.
CI can be run on a pushed branch before it lands on main.
acceptance: Push a commit → four test shards run and all must pass for a green result.
Attempt a CI release on a commit whose CI failed → refused with the reason.

cards.title: Packaged builds are smoke-tested before they are published
cards.user_does: Nothing; runs as part of a release.
cards.user_sees: A broken build never reaches users: the release stops if the packaged app fails its checks.
rules: CLI smoke: the packaged CLI's version matches the release, help works, and the old-profile migration works in an isolated profile.

Terminal smoke: the packaged app starts hidden in a throwaway profile with its own terminal service, draws coloured output, round-trips a clipboard copy, opens 16 panes without falling back from GPU rendering, and tests WSL when present.
The terminal smoke runs only in the older tag-triggered pipeline; the automatic release runs the CLI smoke.
acceptance: Break the packaged CLI version → release stops before publishing.

cards.title: A manual restore check proves terminals survive quits and a killed service
cards.user_does: Runs the restore check against a packaged build.
cards.user_sees: A pass or fail for: folder workspaces with markers in their panes survive three quit-relaunch cycles, then a killed isolated terminal service and a cold restore.
rules: Uses an isolated profile and only kills its own terminal service.
Not wired into the automatic release; run by hand.
acceptance: Run the check on a good build → all four relaunches show the markers.

cards.title: Tag-triggered CI release pipeline
cards.user_does: Pushes a version tag.
cards.user_sees: CI builds, creates a draft release first, publishes the installer, runs both smoke tests and only then marks it latest.
rules: The tag must equal the project version.
Superseded by the automatic release on every ship; tagging is now discouraged because it starts paid CI.
acceptance: n/a — decision item

cards.title: Code-signed installers (opt-in, off)
cards.user_does: Installs a release.
cards.user_sees: Releases are unsigned unless signing is switched on at build time.
rules: Builds before mid-September carried a signer name and need one manual reinstall before auto-update works.
Signing and in-app rollback are planned but unshipped.
acceptance: n/a — decision item

cards.title: Development copy: lighter dev server, clean exit, DEV identity
cards.user_does: A developer runs the app from source.
cards.user_sees: The dev server uses about half the memory, exits when the shell that started it dies, the copy is labelled DEV with its branch, and first-run education is suppressed; startup timing can be printed by an environment flag.
rules: Main-process source maps are skipped in dev to save memory.
The dev parent watches its launching shell and shuts down when it goes.
acceptance: n/a — decision item

cards.title: Leftover data from the retired OpenCode integration is removed at startup
cards.user_does: Launches after upgrading from a version that supported OpenCode.
cards.user_sees: Nothing; old OpenCode files are cleaned up.
rules: Only the retired integration's own files are touched.
acceptance: n/a — decision item

cards.title: Headless serve mode with a virtual display
cards.user_does: Runs the app as a headless server for remote clients.
cards.user_sees: The app runs without a window, optionally on a virtual display, and answers remote clients.
rules: Dropped with area 18 together with the serve command.
acceptance: n/a — decision item

cards.title: Remote sessions reconnect at startup; remote clipboard and mobile relays
cards.user_does: Launches with SSH workspaces open, or pastes files into a remote terminal.
cards.user_sees: SSH connections restore at startup; pasted files are staged on the remote host; markdown requests relay to mobile.
rules: Dropped with area 18.
acceptance: n/a — decision item
cards.decision: default cut: SSH, remote clipboard staging and mobile relays went with area 18. Revive via DECISIONS.md.

cards.title: WSL command reconciliation at startup
cards.user_does: Launches with WSL projects.
cards.user_sees: Startup waits for WSL tool detection; landing checks probe WSL.
rules: Dropped with WSL execution in area 18.
acceptance: n/a — decision item
cards.decision: default cut: WSL execution went with area 18. Revive via DECISIONS.md.

cards.title: The user's work stays on the computer and the app sends no usage data
cards.user_does: Uses Kolux normally: types in terminals, opens files, saves keys, runs agents, sends feedback.
cards.user_sees: Nothing about their work leaves the machine on the app's behalf. Feedback and crash reports open in the user's own browser for them to submit; the app's privacy statement lists every outbound path.
rules: No usage telemetry, analytics or diagnostic upload is sent; the build has no server to send them to.
Typed input, opened files, terminal output, projects, settings and saved credentials are kept only in the local profile folder.
Agent CLIs talk to their own providers under their own accounts; the app neither proxies nor logs that traffic.

The app itself contacts only: GitHub Releases for update checks, downloads and release notes; the git remotes and GitHub account the user configured; AI providers the user connected, with the user's own credentials; and sites the user opens in the browser pane.
Send Feedback and Report Crash never submit anything themselves; the browser does, after the user reviews it.
acceptance: Run a normal session with a network monitor → every connection the app opens belongs to one of the listed destinations; none goes to an analytics or telemetry host.
Type a unique marker string in a terminal and an editor → it appears in no outbound request.
Send Feedback → the browser opens a pre-filled issue page and the app itself makes no request.
evidence: cards-raw/19-app-lifecycle.json D-19-045 (telemetry compiled off), D-19-037 (feedback via browser), D-19-024 (update source)

notes: Brief says 15-minute update checks; code at 0.15.0 checks every 30 minutes (changed 2026-10-05). Cards use 30 minutes; the HANDOFF and release reference still mention daily checks against the private repo, which is stale.
Daemon generations, Resource Manager UI and CLI memory/open/status are mostly tested in areas 03, 05 and 20; carded here per the area 19 row with related set. Expect duplicates when merging.
Release channels (RC, perf, hourly, daily, ad hoc) and local-build switching look inherited from upstream; Kolux publishes one channel, so they are probably unreachable. Carded H.
Windows signature security stop is likely unreachable because current releases are unsigned (carded P2, live-unverified).
Linux and macOS paths (package recovery, AppImage, press-and-hold, Full Disk Access, menu-bar icon, hang watchdog) only reach users if those platforms are ever released; carded H.
Keep-awake setting: macOS and Linux implementations confirmed from tests; Windows behaviour UNKNOWN.
Dev-server memory halving and exit-with-shell are backed by commits a95dccb62 and 50c8c5173 (2026-10-05) and one test file, with no recorded measurement.
Release reference line counts and HANDOFF entries were read at 0.15.0; anything shipped after 2026-10-06 is not reflected.

Critic r1 (2026-10-06): D-19-005 re-tiered P0 live -> H hidden (no UI or CLI caller opens a session window; duplicate of D-03-124). New D-19-070 privacy promise from README Privacy section. Rule lines added to D-19-002, 004, 006, 009, 011, 015, 017, 026, 032, 038, 040, 042, 048, 060.

Critic r1 suggestion for area 03: D-03-119 (shell history per worktree) lacks the history clean-up rule: history of removed worktrees is pruned, folder workspaces and other profiles are kept, and nothing is pruned when any profile is unreadable (src/main/window/history-gc-worktree-ids.ts).

Critic r2 (2026-10-06): no new cards from the fresh sample (76 mapped, 11 drop, 7 not user-facing, 6 other area). Fix: D-19-070 tier P1 -> P0 (pushed 5 is a top-5 theme, so the tier rule makes it P0). Rule lines added to D-19-004, 019, 020, 029, 031 (x3), 035, 036, 038 (x2), 041, 048 (x2, related 05 added), 054. Critic r2 suggestions for other areas (behaviour seen in area 19 test files, not carded here): area 05 sidebar worktree card always keeps the status and unread properties on top of the ones the user picks (src/main/persistence-ui-state.test.ts:658); area 02/03 a new session's start-up command is delivered as a bracketed paste only when the shell is known to handle it, otherwise typed raw with a trailing submit (src/shared/startup-command-submission.test.ts:43); area 03 D-03-119 still lacks the shell-history clean-up rule noted in r1; area 17 keybindings warn about macOS system shortcut conflicts by physical digit-row key, layout-aware (src/shared/macos-symbolic-hotkeys.test.ts).
